independent.summary: `/health` is mounted after the `express-session` middleware, which in production is backed by `MongoStore` (its own MongoClient). A poll that carries any session cookie therefore hits `store.get` before the route runs: with Mongo unreachable — the exact state the endpoint exists to report — that lookup blocks until server selection times out (~30s) and then `express-session` calls `next(err)`, so the caller gets a 500 from `errorHandler` instead of the 503 `degraded`. The suite can't catch it because it injects a `MemoryStore` and sends no cookie; mounting the router ahead of `app.use(session(...))` would make the route independent of the store.

grades.reason: The dedicated HEAD test does assert emptiness — `assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(res.body), [], 'a HEAD carries no body')` (health.test.js:178-179); the later HEAD probe in the degraded case only re-checks the status code, and Express strips bodies on HEAD anyway.

triageGrades.reason: The change deliberately alters the authentication boundary: it adds the app's first new unauthenticated mount ahead of `requireAuth` in `createApp` (app.js:133), and the test asserts it answers with no session or cookie while `/entities` still 401s.
No credentials, tokens or env secrets are added or exposed — the body is deliberately restricted to status/db/uptimeSeconds with no version, commit or provider names.
No billing, pricing or paid-API usage anywhere in the diff; outbound providers are explicitly out of scope.
The route is read-only (reads `mongoose.connection.readyState`) and writes no documents; the test's `mongoose.disconnect()`/`connect()` only cycles the harness connection.
No outbound calls are made or changed; checking AI providers and other external dependencies is explicitly excluded.
No deploy or release config is touched — only a route, a mount, tests and docs; pointing the host's healthcheck at `/health` is left as a dashboard change.

summary: The local review produced one finding that is plainly false (the HEAD body emptiness is asserted in the file it cites), missed the only real gap (the Mongo-backed session store sitting in front of the endpoint that is supposed to answer when Mongo is down), and got the triage right except for calling an explicitly auth-bypassing new public mount "auth: not touched".
